intended_object: The definition is a helper for the proof of `toPontryaginDual_surjective`. Given a character χ of the restricted product Πʳ [X i, U i], it gives the unique y_i ∈ Y i whose local character x ↦ e_i(x, y_i) equals the restriction of χ to the i-th coordinate copy of X i. I inferred this from the docstring and from how the surjectivity proof uses it.
explanation:
The body takes the inverse of the bijection Y i → Hom(X i, Circle) built from the bicharacter e i (bijectivity is passed in as `hperfect`). It applies that inverse to the local character `coordinateCharacter U χ i`, which is χ composed with the i-th single-coordinate embedding. The lemma `reconstructedCoordinate_spec` confirms that this is the intended behaviour: e i x (reconstructedCoordinate … χ i) = χ (mulSingle U i x).

Its only role is as an intermediate step in proving surjectivity. That proof builds the preimage of χ coordinate by coordinate and then shows that the resulting family is restricted. It is not a standard mathematical notion that would be stated or generalised on its own; at most it is the i-th coordinate of the preimage of χ under the duality map, written out for the proof's convenience. So it is an auxiliary proof device, not a mathematical object. The construction itself is correct for that purpose.
